subject: Novalabs preflight: throughput forecast + temporary throttle carveout request
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 9 May 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Novalabs preflight: throughput forecast + temporary throttle carveout request

Team — looping you in on a Novalabs launch that just moved up. Key asks below; I put the forecast in the attached spreadsheet (novalabs_traffic_estimates.xlsx).

Quick context:
- Account: Novalabs (trial -> paid pilot). They run an AI-assistant that will hit Redwood via our hosted API.
- Launch window: planned ramp next Monday (2028-05-15), with a 48-hour high-traffic window following the ramp.
- Commercial: expect to convert during pilot if launch metrics are met; deal id D-4581.

Asks (priority order):
1) Temporary throughput carveout: Customer asks for a temporary increase to their per-minute token allowance for the 48-hour post-launch window to avoid self-throttling during the spike. We need product/ops approval on the magnitude (see sheet: peak QPS and token mix).
2) Product asks: confirm whether we can apply a routing policy that prefers a dedicated warm pool for Novalabs traffic for that window (even if it means short-term burst allocation).
3) Engineering: quick sanity check on warmup steps (KV cache warm windows, recommended model variant) and any constraints that would block a carveout this close to launch.

Notes:
- The estimates include a 3x safety multiplier on session peak. The customer says peak sessions will occur in two 2-hour blocks (10:00-12:00 and 18:00-20:00 PDT).
- They can tolerate slightly higher latency (200-300ms p50) during those blocks but want no 429s.

Attachments: novalabs_traffic_estimates.xlsx (sheet: per-min token forecast, seq-len distro).

Can you each reply with: (A) feasibility, (B) an actionable guardrail (max tokens/min we can offer safely, or alternative), and (C) any docs/forms needed (SLA exception, procurement). I want to consolidate and respond to Elena by EOD tomorrow.

— Irene
Irene Choi
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
irene@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 9 May 2028 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Novalabs preflight: throughput forecast + temporary throttle carveout request

Thanks, Irene — I reviewed the attached sheet quickly. A couple quick clarifying questions before we commit to any carveout: 

1) Token mix: are the user messages heavier on input tokens or output tokens? The sheet's "avg token/session" looks like it's output-heavy (suggests long generations). If the spike is output-dominant, that has a larger cost and scheduling impact.
2) Peak shape: the 3x safety multiplier is good, but can Novalabs confirm whether traffic is uniform across their fleet or concentrated from a specific workspace/region? Concentration -> higher risk of hotspot-induced slowdowns.
3) Control plane: will they accept a fallback policy to a smaller model variant if we hit a platform-level congestion threshold? If yes, we can avoid a higher-cost dedicated pool.

If the answers: output-heavy + concentrated traffic + no fallback, we should prefer provisioning a temporary dedicated warm pool and file an SLA-exception. That will require sign-off from finance for the short-term commit.

Irene — please ask Elena for the three quick confirmations and also ask them to fill the SLA-exception-form.pdf (attached in my reply once Marcus confirms feasibility).

— Marissa
Director, Product — Redwood Console

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 May 2028 10:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Novalabs preflight: throughput forecast + temporary throttle carveout request

Quick tech readout (short):

Feasibility: doable, but with constraints. I attached a short "capacity-impact-estimate.pdf" that outlines token/sec implications for the requested window. Key points:
- Warm pool vs hosted routing: We can carve out a temporary dedicated warm pool for Novalabs for 48 hours, but it requires a manual reservation of capacity and may push other burstable customers into the shared pool. Net risk: elevated shared-pool latency if multiple customers spike concurrently.
- Alternative (lower risk): keep them on hosted but apply a lighter temporary per-customer cap uplift + aggressive KV prefix caching plus model-variant fallback to keep 429s low. This reduces cost/dedicated friction.
- Technical requirements: We need 24 hours lead time to provision and warm GW caches to reach steady-state KV hit rates (especially for the 2-hour concentrated peaks).

Recommended guardrail (if we choose non-dedicated uplift):
- Increase tokens/min by +150% during the 48-hour window, with a hard ceiling of 2.5M tokens/min across the account. If platform telemetry shows p95 latency > 1s or error rate > 0.5% we automatically revert back and trigger an on-call page.

If we provision dedicated capacity: we can guarantee no 429s for the window but need: (A) finance approval for the short-term capacity cost, (B) ops runbook (I can draft), (C) SLA-exception-form completed and signed.

Attaching: capacity-impact-estimate.pdf. I'll follow up with an ops runbook snippet (warm steps + KV warmup checklist).

— Marcus
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena@novalabs.io>, Novalabs Ops <ops@novalabs.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 May 2028 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Novalabs preflight: throughput forecast + temporary throttle carveout request

Elena — thanks again for the quick turn on the timeline. Internal team has reviewed and we have two viable options. Please confirm which you prefer by EOD Monday so we can finalize provisioning.

Option A — Dedicated warm pool (recommended if you want zero-429 risk):
- Redwood provisions a temporary dedicated warm pool for 48 hours following your ramp.
- Pros: No 429s, controlled latency profile; consistent performance.
- Cons: Higher short-term cost; requires a signed SLA exception and a short billing addendum.
- Requirements from Novalabs: sign SLA-exception-form.pdf (attached) and confirm the final peak QPS numbers in the attached spreadsheet.

Option B — Hosted uplift + safe guards (lower cost, slightly higher risk):
- We apply a temporary +150% tokens/min uplift with a hard ceiling at 2.5M tokens/min for your account during the 48-hour window.
- We enable aggressive prefix/KV caching and a fallback to a smaller model variant if platform congestion triggers our safety thresholds.
- Pros: Lower cost, faster to enable (can be done within ~6 hours), does not require capacity reservation.
- Cons: We cannot absolutely guarantee zero 429s under extreme multi-customer contention.

Next steps / mutual action plan:
1) Novalabs to confirm option A or B and sign the SLA-exception-form.pdf if A.
2) Novalabs to finalize the per-minute token forecast and confirm concentration (single-region vs distributed) — see novalabs_traffic_estimates.xlsx, column "peak_region_share".
3) If A, Redwood will provision and begin warmup 24 hours prior to ramp; Marcus will lead the warmup checklist.
4) If B, Redwood will apply uplift and monitor; we will revert automatically if p95 latency > 1s or error rate > 0.5%.

Links/attachments: novalabs_traffic_estimates.xlsx, capacity-impact-estimate.pdf, SLA-exception-form.pdf, and a DocuSign link (https://docusign.example/ND-4581) for the SLA exception (if needed).

Elena — can you confirm which option you prefer and attach a signed SLA-exception (if A) by EOD Monday? We will block preliminary capacity on Tuesday once we receive confirmation.

Thanks — Irene
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
